summaryBox.title: First-Order Integrated Kinetics
summaryBox.takeaway: ln([A]₀/[A]_t) = kt; [A]_t = [A]₀ e^(-kt). Plot of ln[A]_t vs t has slope = -k; plot of log₁₀[A]_t vs t has slope = -k / 2.303.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FIRST-ORDER INTEGRATED KINETICS
                       
   Differential Rate Law:  $-\frac{d[A]}{[A]} = k \cdot dt$
   Integration:            $$\mathbf{\ln \left( \frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right) = k t} \implies \mathbf{k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log_{10} \left( \frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right)}$$
   Exponential Form:       $$\mathbf{[A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}}$$

                        FIRST-ORDER GRAPHICAL PLOTS
                        
        ln [A]_t ▲                              log₁₀ [A]_t ▲
                 │ * (y-intercept = ln [A]₀)                 │ * (y-intercept = log₁₀ [A]₀)
                 │  \                                        │  \
                 │   \  Slope = -k                           │   \  Slope = -k / 2.303
                 │    \
               0 └─────*───────────► Time (t)              0 └─────*───────────► Time (t)
conceptBreakdown.content:
A First-Order Reaction is one where the reaction rate is directly proportional to the first power of reactant concentration:
$$\text{Reaction: } A \longrightarrow \text{Products} \quad \implies \quad \text{Rate} = -\frac{d[A]}{dt} = k [A]$$

$$\mathbf{\ln \left( \frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right) = k t} \implies \mathbf{k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log_{10} \left( \frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right)} \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbf{[A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Half-Life & Fractional Completion for First-Order
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Half-Life & Fractional Completion for First-Order
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
FIRST-ORDER FRACTIONAL TIMELINES
                        
   Amount Remaining ($[A]_t$) after $n$ half-lives:  $$\mathbf{[A]_t = [A]_0 \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^n = [A]_0 \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^{t / t_{1/2}}}$$
   
   ├── $t_{75\%}   = t_{3/4}  = 2 \times t_{1/2}$  ($75\%$ completed, $25\%$ remaining)
   ├── $t_{87.5\%} = t_{7/8}  = 3 \times t_{1/2}$  ($87.5\%$ completed, $12.5\%$ remaining)
   └── $t_{99.9\%} \approx 10 \times t_{1/2}$     ($99.9\%$ completed, $0.1\%$ remaining)

  - Radioactive Decay Parallelism: All natural and artificial nuclear decay processes strictly follow first-order kinetics (\lambda = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}).
conceptBreakdown.content:
Setting $[A]_t = \frac{[A]_0}{2}$ in the integrated rate law:
$$\mathbf{t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693147}{k}}$$

- **Key Invariance Property**: The half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of a first-order reaction is completely **INDEPENDENT of initial concentration $[A]_0$**.
- **Radioactive Decay Parallelism**: All natural and artificial nuclear decay processes strictly follow first-order kinetics ($\lambda = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$).

quickRevision: All nuclear decay processes strictly follow first-order kinetics.
